steps.title: 2013: two proposals
text: In September 2013, at Nazarbayev University in [Kazakhstan](KAZ), Xi Jinping proposed a **Silk Road Economic Belt**; in October, in [Indonesia](IDN)'s parliament, a **21st-Century Maritime Silk Road**. Together they became the Belt and Road Initiative.

The dashed outline marks the **156 countries** that [China](CHN)'s official Belt and Road Portal lists as having signed cooperation documents. [Italy](ITA) withdrew in 2023 and [Panama](PAN) in 2025. The same countries are used for every year, so earlier and later years compare like with like.

steps.title: A growing share of China's exports
text: In 2012 these countries bought **37%** of the [Chinese mainland](CHN)'s goods exports. By 2024 they bought **48%**, and in 2025 about half.
From 2012 to 2024 China's exports to them grew **129%**, from $758 billion to $1.73 trillion, against 43% to all other countries.

steps.title: A shift that began earlier
text: The rise did not start in 2013. The same countries' share of [China](CHN)'s exports grew from 24% in 2000 to 37% in 2012, about **1.1 points a year**, and by about 1 point a year after 2013.
So the data shows a long shift towards these markets that continued under the initiative, rather than a break in 2013.

steps.title: What China buys and sells
text: Partner countries supply most of [China](CHN)'s raw materials: **96%** of its crude oil imports in 2024, 88% of its copper ore and 73% of its soybeans (the list includes [Russia](RUS), [Saudi Arabia](SAU), [Iraq](IRQ) and [Brazil](BRA)).

China sells them more manufactured goods: their share of its machinery and electronics exports rose from 32% to 42% between 2012 and 2024, and its car exports to them from $4.0 billion to $53.3 billion.

steps.title: Loans
text: Partner countries' public external debt owed to lenders in [China](CHN) rose from **$64 billion** in 2012 to a peak of **$189 billion** in 2021, then fell to $170 billion in 2024. In 2012 they owed more to [Japan](JPN) ($103 billion); by 2024 they owed China twice as much as Japan ($83 billion).

Overall, China holds **7.5%** of these countries' public external debt, but it is concentrated: about half in the [Republic of Congo](COG) (56%), [Laos](LAO) (53%) and [Djibouti](DJI) (51%). The map shows China's share of each country's public external debt.

steps.title: Investment
text: Direct investment from the [Chinese mainland](CHN) in partner countries reached **$313 billion** in 2024, up from $187 billion in 2018, the first year China reports by destination. The largest stocks are in [Singapore](SGP) ($85.8 billion), [Indonesia](IDN), [Thailand](THA) and [Cambodia](KHM).

That is only **18%** of the $1.78 trillion China reports abroad: most is recorded in financial centres such as [Hong Kong](HKG), the British Virgin Islands and the Cayman Islands, from where it may be invested elsewhere.

steps.title: What this data can't show
text: These statistics show trade, debt and investment stocks, not projects. Ports, railways and power plants financed by [China](CHN) are tracked project by project elsewhere, for example by AidData (20,985 projects in 165 countries, 2000–2021).

Trends before and after 2013 show what changed, not what caused it. Turn the highlight off or on above, or open Compare with “Share of public external debt owed to China (mainland)” to explore further.
